mcqs.learning_point: Recognise that compounds have fixed composition
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best compares a pure compound with a mixture regarding their composition?

options.A: Both have a fixed ratio of atoms in their constituent particles.
options.B: A compound has a fixed composition of elements, whereas a mixture can have varying proportions of its components.
options.C: In a mixture, the elements are chemically bonded, while in a compound they are only physically combined.
options.D: Compounds and mixtures both have variable composition depending on external conditions.

mcqs.answer: A compound has a fixed composition of elements, whereas a mixture can have varying proportions of its components.
mcqs.explanation: Compounds consist of atoms of different elements chemically combined in a definite ratio, giving them a fixed composition. Mixtures are physical combinations where the relative amounts of the components can vary, so their composition is not fixed.

mcqs.question: In a competitive examination, a student is asked to select the correct statement about compounds and mixtures. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Compounds can be separated into their constituent elements by physical methods, whereas mixtures require chemical methods.
options.B: Compounds have a definite composition and fixed chemical properties, while mixtures have no fixed composition and their properties depend on the proportion of components.
options.C: Both compounds and mixtures have the same boiling point as the pure substances they contain.
options.D: In a mixture, the constituent substances are chemically bonded, unlike in a compound where they are only physically mixed.

mcqs.answer: Compounds have a definite composition and fixed chemical properties, while mixtures have no fixed composition and their properties depend on the proportion of components.
mcqs.explanation: A compound's atoms are chemically bonded in a specific ratio, giving it a constant composition and characteristic properties. Mixtures are physical blends; their overall composition can vary, and their properties change with the relative amounts of the constituents. The other options reverse these facts.

mcqs.question: How is an element defined in chemistry?

options.A: A substance that can be broken down into simpler substances by chemical reactions.
options.B: A pure substance that consists of only one type of atom and cannot be chemically decomposed into simpler substances.
options.C: A combination of two or more elements chemically bonded in a fixed ratio.
options.D: A mixture of different substances that can be separated by physical means.

mcqs.answer: A pure substance that consists of only one type of atom and cannot be chemically decomposed into simpler substances.
mcqs.explanation: An element is a pure substance made up of identical atoms. By definition, it cannot be broken down into simpler substances through chemical reactions. Options A, C, and D describe compounds or mixtures, not elements.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a chemical compound?

options.A: A pure substance made of only one kind of atom.
options.B: A mixture of two or more substances that can be separated by filtration.
options.C: A substance formed when two or more elements combine in a fixed proportion and are chemically bonded.
options.D: A collection of atoms that are not chemically bonded.

mcqs.answer: A substance formed when two or more elements combine in a fixed proportion and are chemically bonded.
mcqs.explanation: A compound results from a chemical reaction between elements, producing a new substance with a definite composition and chemical bonds. Option A describes an element, B describes a mixture, and D contradicts the definition of a compound.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an element from a compound?

options.A: Elements consist of two or more types of atoms, whereas compounds consist of only one type of atom.
options.B: Elements can be broken down into simpler substances by chemical reactions, while compounds cannot.
options.C: Elements are pure substances made of identical atoms; compounds are pure substances composed of two or more different elements chemically combined in fixed ratios.
options.D: Both elements and compounds have variable composition depending on the source.

mcqs.answer: Elements are pure substances made of identical atoms; compounds are pure substances composed of two or more different elements chemically combined in fixed ratios.
mcqs.explanation: Elements contain only one kind of atom and cannot be chemically decomposed. Compounds contain two or more different elements chemically bonded in a definite proportion. Options A, B, and D misrepresent these definitions.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise that compounds have fixed composition
mcqs.question: A sample of pure water (H₂O) is analyzed and found to contain 2 hydrogen atoms for every 1 oxygen atom. Which principle does this observation illustrate?

options.C: Fixed composition of compounds, meaning compounds always contain elements in a definite ratio.

mcqs.answer: Fixed composition of compounds, meaning compounds always contain elements in a definite ratio.
mcqs.explanation: Water always contains hydrogen and oxygen in the 2:1 atomic ratio, demonstrating that a compound has a fixed composition. The law of multiple proportions deals with different compounds of the same elements, and the other options are unrelated.

mcqs.question: Consider two samples: (i) Table salt (NaCl) and (ii) A mixture of sand and salt. Which of the following correctly compares these two regarding composition and separation methods?

options.A: Both have fixed composition and can be separated only by chemical reactions.
options.B: Sample (i) has a fixed composition and can be separated into Na and Cl only by chemical means; sample (ii) has variable composition and its components can be separated by physical methods such as sieving.
options.C: Sample (i) has variable composition, while sample (ii) has a fixed composition of sand and salt.
options.D: Both are mixtures and can be separated by simple filtration.

mcqs.answer: Sample (i) has a fixed composition and can be separated into Na and Cl only by chemical means; sample (ii) has variable composition and its components can be separated by physical methods such as sieving.
mcqs.explanation: Table salt is a compound with a definite Na:Cl ratio; separating Na and Cl requires chemical reactions. The sand‑salt mixture is a physical mixture; its components retain their original identities and can be separated by physical means like sieving or filtration. Options A, C, and D incorrectly describe the nature of the substances.

mcqs.question: A student finds a pure gold nugget and wonders if it is an element. Based on the definition of an element, which statement is true about the gold nugget?

options.A: It is a compound because it contains gold atoms bonded with other atoms.
options.B: It is an element because it consists entirely of gold atoms and cannot be chemically broken down into simpler substances.
options.C: It is a mixture because it may contain trace amounts of other minerals.
options.D: It is a solution because gold can dissolve in water.

mcqs.answer: It is an element because it consists entirely of gold atoms and cannot be chemically broken down into simpler substances.
mcqs.explanation: Gold is a chemical element; a pure nugget contains only gold atoms. Elements cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means. Options A, C, and D misclassify gold as a compound, mixture, or solution.
